IncidentBot: PAGER: [P1] auth-service -> sudden 401 spike in prod (05:12:03 UTC). High request volume from suspicious IPs. Alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/6054321987. @Jamie is primary oncall.
Jamie: On it — joining triage. I’ll collect initial scope.
Olivia: Any customer-facing 5xx/timeout errors or just 401s?
Jamie: Only 401s so far. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/auth/refresh. Error rate +18% over 2m. No customer tickets yet.
Mike: IPs: 45.77.12.0/24 and 185.67.99.101. Looks like credential stuffing using svc tokens. Recommend immediate token revocation and WAF block.
Jamie: Running quick query: `top_ips = logs| where service=="auth" and status==401 | count() by ip | sort desc | limit 10` -> top ips match Mike. Sample headers show `Authorization: Bearer svc-...` fragments.
Darren: Hmm — we changed log-forwarder yesterday. Possible debug dump to staging bucket. I'll check S3 write jobs.
Sara: If tokens leaked, CS needs a heads-up. I can draft customer-safe language. Any confirmed exfil?
Olivia: Not confirmed yet. I see a failed logforwarder job to s3://redwood-staging-logs/debug/2026-03-17 that contains a few auth header lines. Darren, can you confirm object exists?
Darren: Confirmed: `debug/2026-03-17-03T22Z.log` present, ~1.2k lines. Contains several lines with bearer tokens that map to active svc tokens. Marking object quarantined and reducing public access now.
Mike: Escalate plan: 1) Revoke all `svc-*` tokens issued in last 30d. 2) Block offending IP ranges at WAF and edge. 3) Quarantine suspect logs & preserve for forensics. 4) Check CI/CD artifact uploads for exposures. Who can run the rotation?
Jamie: I’ll coordinate. Darren, can you run revocation + reissue (rolling) and post status? I’ll apply temporary WAF blocks and hotpatch routing rules to rate-limit auth endpoints.
Darren: Starting rotation run: `./tools/token-rotate --filter "svc-*" --since 30d --dry-run=false`. Kicking off now. Will post counts.
IncidentBot: ACTION: token-rotate started by Darren at 05:15:40 UTC. WAF rules applying for 45.77.12.0/24 and 185.67.99.101.
Olivia: After WAF block, auth spike is trending down. Monitor for retries/backoff storms.
Sara: Drafting customer note: "We detected suspicious attempts using leaked service credentials. We rotated affected tokens and blocked malicious IPs. No customer data exfiltration confirmed. Investigation ongoing — we'll update within 24 hours." Sending to Legal for review.
Mike: Also add follow-ups: S3 ACL audit, restrict log-forwarder role to narrow permissions, scan recent CI logs for tokens, rotate any k8s secrets referencing rotated tokens.
Jamie: Good. I'll add a console rollout to restart pods that mount affected secrets to ensure no old tokens persist.
Darren: Rotation finished — revoked 14 tokens, reissued 14 replacements, restarted 12 pods that used those tokens. Quarantined log object and copied to secure forensic bucket. WAF blocks are in place.
Olivia: Metrics stable, 401 rate back to baseline. No new suspicious IP activity detected.
Mike: Filing an internal remediation ticket with checklist: ACL audit, pipeline secret scan, lock down forwarder role, add redact filter to log-forwarder.
Sara: Customer note approved by Legal. Sending out now.
Legal: Reviewed. Keep the statement tight; avoid saying "no exfiltration" as final — say "no evidence of customer data exfiltration so far."
Jamie: Thanks team. Closing pager for now. If anything else pops up reopen. :thumbsup:
